subject: FintechCo \u0014 pricing & region residency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo  pricing & region residency follow-up

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the call today  really useful to walk through FintechCo's planned workload and residency constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap (from today's conversation):
- Expected steady-state inference volume: ~1.0B tokens / month (generation + few-shot prompts)
- Embeddings: ~200M vectors / month (batching expected)
- Regional split: ~70% US / 30% EU (EU data residency required for EU customer data)
- Peak concurrency: bursts up to ~40k token QPS for short windows
- Initial commercial preference: hosted API to start, possible move to Dedicated in Q4 if committed volumes materialize
- Procurement contact: Priya Iyer (CC'd)

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) Unit economics: target $/1M tokens you have in mind (you mentioned wanting to see numbers down to $10$15/1M for committed scenarios).
2) Impact of EU data residency on pricing (is a regional pricing premium acceptable?).
3) Procurement timeline & required paperwork (SOW, security questionnaire).

Attached: initial pricing estimate and a draft SOW so procurement/legal can review.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send a quick unit-economics breakdown (US on-demand vs EU on-demand vs Dedicated reserved capacity) by EOD tomorrow.
- If those look okay, propose a 30m follow-up with Sean (CC) to run through the committed-capacity math and procurement path.

Would you confirm the volumes above and whether the 70/30 US/EU split is representative of production traffic (vs. beta)? That will materially affect the pricing mix we model.

Thanks,

-- 
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
redwood.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo  pricing & region residency follow-up

Thanks Marissa  helpful recap. Confirming the numbers on our side:
- Steady-state: we expect roughly 1.0B tokens/mo in production after the pilot. Pilot month could be ~200300M tokens.
- Embeddings: correct, ~200M vectors/mo (approx 128-d vectors from our pipeline).
- Regional split: yes, 70% US / 30% EU for production traffic. EU-resident customer data must remain in EU.
- Peak concurrency: 40k token QPS is our upper bound during end-of-day runs and some user spikes.

A few clarifying Qs: 
1) For hosted API pricing, what’s the delta (in $/1M tokens) for EU region vs US region? We want to model worst-case costs.
2) For committed / Dedicated options, what commitment levels do you assume to hit $10$15 / 1M tokens? (We want to see the right commitment tier to propose internally.)
3) Is there an additional monthly fee or configuration cost for EU-only data residency? Any KMS/HSM entitlements that add cost?

From a budget perspective, leadership is looking for target pricing in the band of $8$12 / 1M tokens (net effective) if we commit to a 12-month reserved plan. If that's not feasible with hosted on-demand, we want to understand what Dedicated pricing would look like and what minimums apply.

Priya will drive procurement steps  Priya, any preferred cadence for vendor docs?

Best,
Alex

--
Alex Turner
Head of Engineering, FintechCo
alex.turner@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechco.com>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo  pricing & region residency follow-up

Alex  great, thanks for the confirmation and the target band. Below is a concise unit-economics breakdown and notes on EU residency fees so you have something concrete to take to leadership. This assumes 1.0B tokens/mo steady-state (we’ll include a pilot vs committed amortization schedule in the formal quote).

High-level pricing scenarios (per 1M tokens):
A) Hosted  On-demand (no commit)
  - US region: $20.00 / 1M tokens
  - EU region: US price + 25% regional premium = $25.00 / 1M tokens
  - Notes: on-demand is simplest but higher unit cost; regional premium reflects additional infra + networking + compliance overhead.

B) Hosted  Reserved (12m, volume-based discounts)
  - Effective blended (70% US / 30% EU): ~ $13.75 / 1M tokens (example tier: 1B tokens committed/mo -> discounts applied)
  - If you commit to 1.5B tokens/mo the blended rate falls toward ~$11 / 1M tokens.

C) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, contractual commit)
  - Typical effective cost at your scale (1B/mo) with a 12m contract: $8.506$10.50 / 1M tokens (depends on model variant, quantization levels, and burst policy)
  - Pros: predictable throughput, cheaper unit economics at scale, control over regional placement (we can run EU-dedicated pools for residency)

Other considerations:
- EU residency add-on: typically a ~2030% uplift on hosted on-demand due to region capacity and data-handling controls. For Dedicated we can colocate capacity in EU to avoid cross-border ingress egress costs  that reduces per-token premium but requires an inter-region capacity commitment (we’ll call this out in the SOW).
- KMS/HSM: If you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), there’s a small monthly entitlement fee and key-usage metering (we’ll include options in the formal quote).
- Embeddings: charged separately at a lower unit; I put embeddings pricing in the attached estimate for reference.

Given leadership's stated target of $8$12 / 1M tokens with a 12-month commit, Dedicated looks like the most viable path to hit the low end of that band. If leadership prefers hosted with a reserved billing tier, a 1.5B/mo commit will get you into the ~1112 / 1M range blended (US+EU).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll convert this note into a formal quote and a commitment-tier worksheet (attached as redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf).
- Sean (copied) will scope Dedicated configuration if you want a separate Dedicated proposal.
- Priya: if you can share procurement contacts / required PO/legal templates, we’ll prep SOW + order form for review (SOW draft attached).

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow 11:0011:30 PT to run through the numbers with Sean and lock the preferred path?

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole
